claim_verdicts.detail: All-time through the post date is $102,270,125.83, within 0.7% of $103M. But it is not 'since 2016'. Payments dated 2016-01-01 onward total $62,849,835.87. Roughly 41% of the money predates 2016.

claim_verdicts.detail: FY2017 onward through 2026-01-21 was $28,730,378.83. All-time now stands at $32,404,181.08.

claim_verdicts.claim: $121,728.16 paid on a single day, January 16, 2025
claim_verdicts.detail: No payment to any of these vendors on 2025-01-16. No row anywhere in the 49-million-row dataset carries amount = 121728.16. No vendor-day in the group sums to between 121,727 and 121,730. The nearest candidate is 2026-01-16: Beyond Independent Living LLC, 13 payments, $172,708.26; group day total $190,165.88.

claim_verdicts.claim: 2020 State Auditor flagged up to $887,225 in unallowable payments
claim_verdicts.detail: OSA report published 2020-09-21, audit period 2016-01-01 to 2018-12-31. MassHealth paid Beyond Healthcare Agency $1,392,917 for 1,945 GAFC claims covering 117 members. Finding 1 states the agency was paid as much as $887,225 for GAFC that appears to be unallowable, having been billed on the same day as Home Health Program services. The post calls these 'fraudulent claims'; the auditor's language is 'appear to be unallowable'.

claim_verdicts.claim: At least 12-15 LLCs and corporations tied to her name
claim_verdicts.detail: The SOC individual search for last name OSAGIEDE returns 101 role records. Naomi / Aderonke Naomi / Naomi A / Naomi Aderonke Osagiede appears as officer, manager, resident agent or SOC signatory on approximately 20 distinct entities.

claim_verdicts.claim: The vast majority were involuntarily dissolved by the SOC
claim_verdicts.verdict: PATTERN HOLDS ON THE SAMPLE CHECKED, 3 OF 3
claim_verdicts.detail: BEYOND MEDICAL EQUIPMENT LLC dissolved 06-30-2017. BEYOND HEALTHCARE AGENCY LLC dissolved 12-29-2023 and revived 09-20-2024. BEYOND INDEPENDENT LIVING INC, the nonprofit, 001309461, dissolved 06-30-2025. The other ~17 entities were not individually checked.

claim_verdicts.claim: Nonprofit charter revoked February 2025 after no annual report 2018-2024
claim_verdicts.detail: SOC records the Date of Involuntary Dissolution for BEYOND INDEPENDENT LIVING INC (001309461) as 06-30-2025, not February 2025. A February 2025 notice is consistent with what the post reproduces, but the charter date is 6/30/2025. The nonprofit was organized 01-10-2018.

claim_verdicts.claim: On January 22, 2020 Beyond Independent Living LLC was registered to 661 Centre St
claim_verdicts.detail: SOC 001421873, BEYOND INDEPENDENT LIVING LLC, Date of Organization 01-22-2020, records address 661 CENTRE ST, BROCKTON MA 02302, resident agent and manager NAOMI EGAH. Confirms both the date and the Egah alias. Note this is a second LLC bearing a name identical to the payee LLC (462941036), which sits in Boston under Osagiede.

new_findings_not_in_the_post.finding: The state paid the audited entity while it was legally dissolved
new_findings_not_in_the_post.detail: Beyond Healthcare Agency LLC was involuntarily dissolved by the SOC on 12-29-2023 and not revived until 09-20-2024. CTHRU shows 153 payments totalling $643,388.39 between 2024-01-08 and 2024-09-16, entirely inside that window.

new_findings_not_in_the_post.finding: Payments continue after the surviving corporate entity was dissolved
new_findings_not_in_the_post.detail: The Beyond Independent Living chain ran LLC 2013 -> profit INC 02-21-2017 -> nonprofit INC 01-10-2018, and ended in involuntary dissolution on 06-30-2025. CTHRU has since paid 'BEYOND INDEPENDENT LIVING LLC' 778 payments totalling $5,908,174.45 from 2025-07-07 through 2026-09-17, all at West Roxbury 02132, the Osagiede address, not the Brockton address held by the separate Egah LLC.

Across all 7,297 payments there is not one negative amount; the minimum amount in the group is $0.21. CAVEAT: MassHealth ordinarily nets recoveries against future claims rather than posting a negative line to the Comptroller's ledger, so this is not proof that nothing was repaid. What it does establish is that no clawback of the $887,225 is visible in the state's own checkbook. The post's public records request is the right next step.

new_findings_not_in_the_post.finding: A second-generation cluster with the same business triad
new_findings_not_in_the_post.detail: SOC lists ERHAUYI OSARUME OSAGIEDE and OMORUYI OSAHON OSAGIEDE as managers of ASCEND ADULT DAY HEALTH LLC (001925121), ASCEND HOME HEALTH AND THERAPY SERVICES LLC (001909915) and ASCEND TRANSPORTATION SERVICES LLC (001979097) — the same adult day health, home health and transport combination. Zero CTHRU payments to date.

new_findings_not_in_the_post.finding: Eighteen other Osagiede entities have never received state money
new_findings_not_in_the_post.detail: A CTHRU sweep of the other ~18 entity names (Beyond Faith Clinic, Beyond Gardens, Beyond Business Management, Greater Healthcare Solutions, Certified Healthcare, Certified Billing Consulting, Medicoach Transportation, Beyond Medical Equipment, Nigerian Nurses Association and the rest) returned no matching vendors. Absence here is not zero: money delivered through a managed care organisation would not appear as a Comptroller disbursement.

$124,799.78 at Methuen and Tewksbury. No Osagiede officer link appears in SOC. Excluded from the verified total.

standing_caveats: CTHRU records Comptroller disbursements. MassHealth fee-for-service claims appear; care paid through managed care organisations and ACOs generally does not. $105.9M is a floor, not a ceiling.
CTHRU appropriation labels such as MANAGED CARE PLAN, MASSHEALTH SENIOR CARE and INDEMNITY/THIRD PARTY LIABILITY PLAN are accounting buckets, not descriptions of the service billed.
Nothing here establishes fraud. An involuntary dissolution is a filing failure. The auditor's phrase 'appear to be unallowable' is an upper-bound estimate, not an adjudicated finding.

Duncan's own repositories (HHS-MA-DOGE, Massachusetts-Data-Hub) contain no reference to any of these entities or to Osagiede. The cluster is absent from data/fraud-detection/elder-homecare-targets.csv even though it would meet that file's own P1 criteria: one person, multiple entities, shared addresses, over $100M billed.
